The Corsair Warthog gaming PC case is a true throwback to an older era of PC building -- when RAM was affordable and NVIDIA hadn't begun its descent into AI psychosis -- and the case does well to bring it back. It has its downsides, but the biggest upside is that it's based on the already well-received Corsair Frame 4000D. We liked the Frame 4000D case in testing, so all of those aspects carry over. The Warthog stops making sense if you're not into its look, especially with the $180 to $200 price point that brings it into competition with a ton of other cases.
